Pri (Product): thanks for the great Q&A today. dropping follow-ups here about a few things folks flagged: org-level pooling, seat-based quotas, and infra/exempt test requests.

Marco (Finance): short summary on pooling: by default credits are scoped to org. We support a "pooled billing" flag for umbrella accounts (multi-org customers) that lets credits be shared across child orgs. It's opt-in and requires a billing agreement change.

Jade (Billing Ops): operational note: pooled billing shows a single balance in the console and an allocation table. We also surface a "per-org burn" breakdown so teams can still track consumption.

Rafi (Support): question that came up from customers: can we exempt internal infra tests from charging?

izzy_dev (eng): we have an internal label mechanism: `x-internal-test: true` header. If the org has "test-exemptions" enabled we will shadow-bill (record usage but not deduct credits). This must be enabled by Billing Ops; it's off by default to avoid abuse.

Jade (Billing Ops): enabling test-exemptions requires: 1) written request from org admin, 2) high-frequency request limits documented, 3) a daily cap. We audit monthly. Abuse cancels the exemption.

Pri (Product): another ask: seat-based quotas — customers want per-user concurrency limits in addition to org-level quotas. Roadmap?

izzy_dev (eng): in backlog: "per-principal quota enforcement" (EA). It will allow org admins to set per-api-key concurrency & rate windows. Works with existing headers: `X-RateLimit-User-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-User-Remaining`.

Marco (Finance): billing nuance: seat-based quotas don't change token billing. They only gate throughput. Billing continues to be per-token or reserved capacity for Dedicated.

Pri (Product): can we have a dry-run enforcement mode so customers can preview which requests would have been blocked?

Jade (Billing Ops): yes — we're shipping "quota-shadow" for EA: it logs enforcement events and returns `X-Quota-Shadow: true` on responses. No 429s are delivered during shadow window. EA sign-up via Product.

Rafi (Support): headers and error body we currently return on hard throttles for hosted: headers: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-Quota-Window`, `Retry-After`, `X-Credit-Balance` (opt-in). Body: `{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","policy":"burst_protection","retry_after_seconds":60}`.

izzy_dev (eng): fallback sequence we use: 1) micro-smoothing (5-30s depending on tier), 2) model-variant fallback if allowed by routing policy, 3) route to lower-priority pool, 4) 429. Customers can reorder or disable steps via `routing_policy` config.

Pri (Product): customers asked about sustained vs burst pricing — will we ever charge differently for bursty spikes?

Marco (Finance): current plan: billing is usage-first (tokens) + capacity for Dedicated. We have no burst premium planned. Instead we offer demo/launch passes and short-term capacity boosts (48-72h). We may offer committed burst packages for enterprise later.

Ava (CEO): high-level: no immediate pricing changes. We want predictable economics for customers — that's why we focus on capacity options, clear headers, and the quota-shadow EA.

LegalBot: reminder: exemptions & pooled billing require updated ToS addendum; Legal will prepare a template for Billing Ops to attach to requests.

Jade (Billing Ops): action items: 1) publish pooled-billing enable guide, 2) bake test-exempt request template, 3) open EA list for quota-shadow.

Pri (Product): I'll draft a short FAQ and a sample client snippet showing header usage + client backoff recipe (respect Retry-After + jitter + honor `X-Quota-Window`). Will post by EOD and ping Support/Engineering for review.

Rafi (Support): I'll prepare customer-friendly KB snippets and examples for the Support triage flow.

izzy_dev (eng): if anyone wants EA access to quota-shadow or per-principal quotas DM me and I'll add you.

Pri (Product): thanks all — closing this thread, will link the FAQ here once live. :thumbsup:
